narrative.overview: LegalLens reads like a page from a bare act: off-white paper, dark ink, a narrow marginal note beside each block of text, and the law itself set in a serif. The one saturated colour, stamp-pad violet, appears only where LegalLens has verified something against the Corpus. Red appears only for what is struck out (a repealed Provision) or has failed. Everything else is ink on paper.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and ink neutrals; violet is rare and meaningful.
Sans for the interface, serif for the law.
Condensed bold headings, after bare-act cover lettering.
Flat surfaces, rules and borders instead of shadows.
One orchestrated motion: the Trust label is stamped onto the answer.

rules.name: The Verified-Only Violet Rule
rules.body: Violet means "checked against the Corpus". It never decorates.

rules.name: The Struck-Out Red Rule
rules.body: Red marks only repealed or failed. Never use it for emphasis or errors of style.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Sans speaks for LegalLens; serif speaks for the law. Never set statute or Contract text in the sans.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are paper, ledger or ruled. Do not add box-shadows or blur.

dos: Do reserve violet for verified content and red for repealed or failed.
Do set law and quotes in the serif at no more than the measure (54ch), with lang="en" on English statute text.
Do keep every theme token defined for light and dark; honour prefers-color-scheme and the saved toggle.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion for every animation.
Do use the glossary terms in copy (Provision, Clause, Citation, Flagged clause).
donts: Don't use shadows, gradients or glass effects.
Don't use red or violet as general emphasis or decoration.
Don't set statute or Contract text in the sans.
Don't word Flagged clauses as "risky" or "red flag", or imply whether to sign.
